## Pull request overview

This PR addresses CI failures by adjusting ObjectCalendar’s mount-time data fetching behavior and making console tests resilient to time/preview behavior changes.

**Changes:**
- Update `ObjectCalendar` to avoid a mount-time double `find()` by removing `objectSchema` from the data-fetch effect dependencies and reading schema via a ref.
- Make calendar integration test data date-relative so events remain within the visible calendar window over time.
- Fix a report live-preview test assertion to validate the updated (live) title rather than the prior title.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx | Changes effect dependencies and introduces an `objectSchemaRef` to prevent duplicate `find()` calls. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/PluginsIntegration.test.tsx | Replaces hardcoded event dates with relative `Date.now()`-based ISO timestamps. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ReportViewConfigPanel.test.tsx | Updates assertion to expect the live-previewed report title after editing. |

Removing `objectSchema` from this dependency array prevents the data-fetch effect from re-running when `setObjectSchema(...)` completes. If `$expand` depends on schema metadata, this means the component can render with incomplete data until some other dependency changes (e.g., refresh). A safer pattern is to keep `objectSchema` as a dependency but early-return when it’s not yet available (so `find()` only executes once, after schema load).

`objectSchemaRef.current` will be `null` on the initial mount (the schema is fetched in a separate effect), so `buildExpandFields(...)` returns an empty array and the first `dataSource.find()` call will not include `$expand`. With `objectSchema` removed from the effect deps, the component will never re-fetch after the schema arrives, so lookup/master_detail fields won’t be expanded until a manual refresh (and if `objectName` changes, the ref may still contain the previous object’s schema, producing an invalid `$expand`). Consider gating the data fetch until the matching object schema has been loaded (or fetching schema + data in a single effect) so the initial request includes the correct `$expand` without reintroducing a double-fetch.
